summary_en.motivation: To investigate the precipitation behavior and its effect on mechanical properties of Sc-modified aluminum alloys fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Aluminum alloys with varying Sc content were fabricated via SLM and characterized by microstructure analysis and mechanical testing.

summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing and microstructure characterization were used to validate the findings.

papers.title: Research on the Thermal Behaviour of a Selectively Laser Melted Aluminium Alloy: Simulation and Experiment
papers.abstract: A 3D Finite Element (FE) model was developed to investigate the thermal behaviour within the melt pool during point exposure to Selective Laser Melting (SLM) processed AlSi10Mg powder. The powder⁻solid transition, temperature-dependent thermal properties, melt pool convection, and recoating phase were taken into account. The effects of Exposure Time (ET) and Point Distance (PD) on SLM thermal behaviour were also investigated and showed that the short liquid phase time and high cooling rate of the melt pool reduced the viscosity of the melt pool at a lower ET or a higher PD. This resulted in poor wettability and the occurrence of balling and micropores. At a higher ET or lower PD the melt pool became unstable and allowed for easy formation of the self-balling phenomenon, as well as further partial remelting in the depth direction resulting in the creation of larger pores. The proper melt pool width (119.8 μm) and depth (48.65 μm) were obtained for a successful SLM process using an ET of 140 μs and a PD of 80 μm. The surface morphologies and microstructures were experimentally obtained using the corresponding processing conditions, and the results aligned with those predicted in the simulation.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the thermal behavior within the melt pool during selective laser melting of AlSi10Mg powder.
summary_en.method: A 3D finite element model incorporating powder-solid transition, temperature-dependent thermal properties, melt pool convection, and recoating was developed.

papers.title: Mussel-Inspired Peptide Coatings on Titanium Implant to Improve Osseointegration in Osteoporotic Condition.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis greatly impairs in vivo implant osseointegration because of poor osteogenesis in osteoporotic conditions and the low bioactivity of implants, such as titanium-based biomaterials. Various surface engineering strategies, including unstable physical absorption or complex chemical conjugations, have been developed to biofunctionalize titanium implants and improve interfacial osseointegration. However, very few of them took into consideration the clinically challenging osteoporotic condition, as well as dual-functionalization of the implants for improvement of both osteoblast adhesion and osteogenesis. In this work, we combined two mussel-inspired bioactive peptides (i.e., with cell adhesive or osteogenic sequences) for one-step dual-functionalization of Ti screws via a facile self-organized multivalent coordinative interaction. In vitro study indicated that the biomimetic dual-functional coating could efficiently improve the osteogenesis of osteoporosis-derived mesenchymal stem cells despite of their impaired bone metabolism. Moreover, under osteoporotic in vivo condition, the dual-functional peptide coating on Ti screws could also give rise to significant enhancement of interfacial osteogenesis, newly formed bone condition, osseointegration, as well as implant mechanical stability. This is probably due to the integrin-targeted cell adhesive and osteogenic motifs on the modified Ti screws, which recovered the regular bone metabolism equilibrium between osteogenesis and osteoclastogenesis in an osteoporotic condition. We anticipate that the highly biomimetic peptides and one-step dual-functionalized strategy would provide a facile and effective means for improving the clinical outcome of Ti-based implants in patients with a disturbed bone metabolism.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于钛植入体的肽涂层以改善骨质疏松条件下的骨整合，完全未涉及增材制造、多孔结构或力学测试，与用户研究方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve additive manufacturing (LPBF), porous structure design, mechanical testing (static or fatigue), or stress shielding analysis, which are core to the AM Biomedical Materials direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 骨质疏松条件下钛植入体骨整合效果差，亟需有效表面改性策略。
summary_zh.method: 利用贻贝启发肽通过自组装一步法双功能化钛钉表面。
summary_zh.result: 双功能肽涂层在体外和体内均显著增强骨整合和植入物稳定性。
summary_zh.validation: 骨质疏松大鼠模型的体内实验及骨质疏松来源干细胞的体外实验。

summary_en.motivation: Osteoporotic bone conditions severely impair implant osseointegration, necessitating surface modifications that promote both cell adhesion and osteogenesis.
summary_en.method: Mussel-inspired bioactive peptides with adhesive and osteogenic sequences were co-assembled onto titanium screws via self-organized multivalent coordination in a one-step process.
summary_en.result: The dual-functional peptide coating enhanced osteogenesis of osteoporosis-derived mesenchymal stem cells in vitro and improved interfacial osseointegration and mechanical stability in an osteoporotic rat model in vivo.
summary_en.validation: In vitro assays using osteoporosis-derived stem cells and in vivo implantation in an osteoporotic rat model with histological and mechanical evaluation.
